# NOTES: Two-book compilation

## BOOK 1 of 2: *The Mystery at Lovers' Cave* (Anthony Berkeley)

Chapters I–XXVI. Narrator: third person, comic detective tone.

**Cast**
- **Roger Sheringham**: novelist, 36, amateur sleuth, writes crime articles for the *Daily Courier*. Editor is "great man"; Burgoyne is the Courier caller. Past case: Wychford / "Hattan Garden jewel case."
- **Anthony Walton**: cousin, 25, big, slow-witted, good-natured. Oxford rugger blue, plays for Harlequins, golf half-blue. Works in father's office. "Idiot friend" per Roger.
- **Mrs. Elsie Vane**: victim, 28, pretty, fair, lisps slightly. Fell from ledge at Ludmouth Bay. Real background: fraudster who married Dr. Vane for money.
- **Dr. George Vane**: husband, much older, scientist/experimentalist. Huge (6'2"), black beard, stern, gentle manner, very courteous. Collects Spode and Dresden china. Has laboratory.
- **Margaret Cross**: cousin, ~22, dark hair in two coils, brown eyes, slim, proud. Father army officer killed in France 1917; mother from Liverpool bucket-shop family. Worked as governess, shop-assistant, waitress, parlour-maid (dismissed after boxing employer's ears). Elsie's will leaves her ~£10,000 plus jewellery.
- **Miss Williamson**: Dr. Vane's secretary/lab assistant. Tall, angular, close-cropped fair hair, pince-nez, Cambridge science degree. In love with George.
- **Inspector Moresby** (Scotland Yard): heavy, grizzled walrus moustache, bland, genial, "butter-knife" face. On holiday in Sandsea with wife and two children. Officially in charge by ch. XII.
- **Mrs. Russell** (and **Mr. Russell**, "John Henry", Rose Cottage): neighbours. Mrs. Russell ~45, fat, pince-nez, large feet, jealous of Elsie. Mr. Russell jolly, red-faced, beefy.
- **Colin Woodthorpe**: 25–26, fair, sanguine, son of Sir Henry Woodthorpe of Clouston Hall (between Ludmouth and Sandsea). Elsie's secret lover (~1 year). Owns a private aeroplane; ex-RAF.
- **Rev. Samuel Meadows**: "goat-faced" little man, silver hair, horn spectacles, claims retired clergyman from Yorkshire. Actually **Herbert Peters** alias **Slippery Sam**, alias The Shrimp, The Sky Pilot, Herbert Smith. Criminal (robbery, burglary, fraud). Former sham husband of Elsie (wartime).
- **Dr. Young**: local doctor, tall, angular, pince-nez.
- **Landlord** of the Crown: big, ox-like. **Landlady** (Mrs. Harper) at Meadows' lodging: stout, chatty. Her husband was a smoker. Mrs. Mullins mentioned.
- **Butler at Clouston Hall**: "dolphin."

**Places**: Waterloo; Bournemouth; Ludmouth (village, one inn, The Crown; station ~1 mile off); Ludmouth Bay (circular inlet, cliffs ~100 ft); Sandsea (6 miles West); Milbourne (village, 2 miles inland); Dr. Vane's red house (~1 mile out toward Sandsea, back from cliffs); Clouston Hall; Pine... (none in Book 1).

**Key objects/clues**
- Footprints: two women's on mud, one larger, high heels. Shoes of a size six fit smaller prints.
- Coat-button: light-blue bone, ~1.5 in, white pattern; clenched in Elsie's right hand. Belongs to Margaret's sports coat; missing when she returned.
- Notepaper found on rocks, watermark a crown. Letter (dated Monday) from "Colin": "Elsie darling, for Heaven's sake meet me once more before you do anything rash... Meet me at the usual place to-morrow, same time... P.S. Destroy this."
- Directory: "Russell, John Henry, Rose Cottage"; Colins: Smith, Colin (plumber, East Row, Ludmouth); Seaford, Colin James (architect, 4 Burnt Oak Lane, Milbourne).
- Mrs. Russell's shoes (size 6, sides slit) found on rock below ledge, after Roger borrowed them from Russells' maid and threw them down.
- Cave: on ledge, mouth at an angle behind a boulder. Contains cigarette-ends (Turkish with pink tips, gaspers), chocolate boxes, banana skins, orange peel, bun, sandwich wrappings, a *London Opinion* (last Saturday's issue).
- Thumbprint: from Meadows' newspaper (Roger's trick).
- Aconitine: found in Meadows' tobacco-jar and pipe stem.
- Handkerchief: cambric with lace, "E" embroidered (Elsie's), left at Meadows' lodgings.

**Timeline of events**
1. Ch I: Roger has breakfast with Anthony in London. Courier phones: Roger sent to Ludmouth. Anthony invited along. They take train from Waterloo; Anthony telegraphs to cancel rooms.
2. Ch II: At Ludmouth inn Roger books all five rooms (£10 deposit). Moresby is staying there. Anthony walks to cliffs and meets Margaret on ledge: "I am Miss Cross."
3. Ch III: Roger meets Moresby on ledge. Footprints shown. Button found. Roger climbs down, pockets paper.
4. Ch IV: Margaret breaks down after Moresby's 2-hour interview. Anthony comforts her. She tells her life story.
5. Ch V: Margaret's account: Elsie went to see Mrs. Russell about a village children's treat, left Margaret waiting on ledge, never returned. Roger & Anthony discuss.
6. Ch VI: Supper with Moresby (gin, whisky, ice). Roger shares clue; Moresby reveals button and footprints. Servants say Elsie and Margaret quarrelled.
7. Ch VII: Anthony and Roger argue. Margaret calls Elsie "loathsome," tells of her bullying, that Elsie married Vane for money. Mrs. Russell's jealousy noted. Roger tests shoes idea.
8. Ch VIII: Meadows (parson-looking) meets Roger on cliffs; long chat. Roger borrows Mrs. Russell's shoes from maid (paid 10 shillings). Shoes fit prints. Mrs. Russell alone at home that afternoon.
9. Ch IX: Letter found. Moresby says "Colin" is not a pet-name. Roger, Anthony, Margaret tea plans. Hand-holding between Anthony and Margaret.
10. Ch X: Tea at Dr. Vane's. Roger praises china; Dr. Vane invites them to supper Sunday. Roger suspects Miss Williamson loves George. Moresby reports he found Colin Woodthorpe.
11. Ch XI: Interview at Clouston Hall. Colin admits affair; says he broke with Elsie at a meeting "a fortnight ago last Tuesday" in the cave. Elsie threatened to tell husband.
12. Ch XII: Moresby reveals Vane family criminal history (great-grandfather burglar, grandfather bucket-shop, Elsie's brother in America a confidence-man). Elsie went through sham wartime marriage with Herbert Peters. Roger & Moresby spar.
13. Ch XIII: Midnight expedition with Anthony to cave: finds *London Opinion* last Saturday's issue and cigarette-ends.
14. Ch XIV: Roger's theory: unknown middle-class man with appointment; maybe Elsie's real husband. Roger meets Meadows on rocks.
15. Ch XV: Roger tests Colin (London Opinion joke): Colin couldn't have left the paper. Anthony & Margaret find shoe on rock; Roger concludes murderer was a man in women's shoes.
16. Ch XVI: Moresby emerges from cave, takes shoe. Moresby suggests Miss Williamson as murderer. Roger tells him everything. Roger gets urchin's witness: man with London Opinion went down steps 3:30pm Tuesday — the man was Meadows.
17. Ch XVII: Roger visits Meadows posing as theologian, gets thumbprint from newspaper. Moresby reveals shoes belonged to Mrs. Russell. Anthony promises secrecy.
18. Ch XVIII: Dinner at Vane's. Moresby's report: thumbprint = Sam Field (Herbert Peters). Warrant planned. Next morning Meadows found dead in chair.
19. Ch XIX: Dr. Young examines body. Roger's indiscreet Courier article leaks details.
20. Ch XX: Inquest adjourned. Aconitine found in tobacco and pipe stem. Moresby: murder.
21. Ch XXI: Roger wonders why Moresby hints at Vane.
22. Ch XXII: Landlady reports night visitor (woman, quarrelling) before Mrs. Vane's death. Handkerchief "E" found. Tobacco shop: Meadows smoked Crown and Anchor Coarse Cut.
23. Ch XXIII: Roger: Mrs. Vane planned trip to friends for "the twelfth." Colin arrives at inn: "I killed Mrs. Vane and—and Meadows."
24. Ch XXIV: Moresby arrives, won't arrest Colin ("boys will be boys"), Colin storms off.
25. Ch XXV: Roger's theory: Mrs. Vane poisoned Meadows in advance with aconitine in pipe; Meadows killed Vane. Roger calls it "The Dead Hand."
26. Ch XXVI: Moresby says Roger's theory wrong. Colin and Margaret have eloped by aeroplane. Moresby says Margaret killed both: button, shoes, aconitine in pipe; she had criminal record. Mrs. Vane's marriage settlement invalid. Ends: "You've been reading too many of those detective stories."

Transcriber's notes: corrections listed (Maragaret→Margaret, Couston→Clouston, etc.).

## BOOK 2 of 2: *Thomas Wingfold, Curate*, Vol II (George MacDonald)

Chapters I–XXXIV. Volume II ends at ch. XXXIV.

**Cast**
- **Thomas Wingfold**: curate at Glaston Abbey, ~30. Doubting, seeking God. Gives unorthodox sermons. Writes sonnets.
- **Rachel Polwarth**: dwarf niece, crooked, cheerful, devout, poetic dreamer. Lies in white room.
- **Mr. Polwarth** (uncle): gatekeeper at Osterfield Park lodge, dwarf, asthmatic, mystic, writes verses and dreams.
- **Helen Lingard**: tall, beautiful, proud, ~mid-20s. Cousin of George; nurses her brother Leopold. Eyes "blue-eyed," pale, weary.
- **Leopold (Poldie) Lingard**: brother, 20, dark tropical complexion (mother was dark-skinned), brain-fever, opium/narcotic habit. Killed his lover **Emmeline** with a knife (they were lovers; she jilted him). Sees her ghost.
- **George Bascombe**: Helen's cousin, barrister, healthy, arrogant materialist; "Hercules Bascombe." Courts Helen.
- **Mrs. Ramshorn**: aunt, widow of the late dean; cold, churchy.
- **Mr. Drew**: linen-draper of Glaston, middle-aged, plump, rosy, pug nose, Methodist-ish deacon. Wife ran off with a traveller ~20 years ago.
- **Dr. Faber**: physician.
- **Mrs. Drew**: runaway wife.
- **Miss Lingard's servants**: maid, butler.

**Places**: Glaston (town with Abbey, churchyard, Pine Street); Osterfield Park; Lingard house (Manor-house); Polwarth cottage; Mr. Drew's shop; Mrs. Ramshorn's house.

**Key objects**: Leather knife sheath (found by Polwarth in old house; dark stain inside lining). Wingfold keeps it; gives to Helen ch XXIII.

**Timeline**
1. Ch I: Helen rides with Miss Lingard (cousin? no—Miss Lingard is a horsewoman, Helen's relation). Rachel and uncle talk about deformity and body; Polwarth reads verses; Rachel's temper; she kisses his hand.
2. Ch II: Polwarth reads poem "Lord, hear my discontent." Wingfold asks about Bible inspiration. Polwarth tells dream: Armenian convent; old John burns the book; "The Word of God liveth... in the heart of the man that in love obeyeth him."
3. Ch III: Wingfold's second sermon "What is Christianity?" (love enemies, be perfect, judge not, do as you would be done by).
4. Ch IV: Mrs. Ramshorn, Bascombe discuss sermon. Helen nursing Leopold; Faber suspects his drug withdrawal. Helen reads Arabian Nights to him.
5. Ch V: Glaston gossip on Wingfold. Poem about signs.
6. Ch VI: Mr. Drew confesses unfair trade; Wingfold says "do as ye would be done by." Drew resolves change.
7. Ch VII: Wingfold brings Drew to Polwarth tea. Rachel talks of dreams.
8. Ch VIII: Sonnet "Methought I floated sightless..."
9. Ch IX: Drew sells print at cost to soldiers' wives; shop as temple.
10. Ch X: Bascombe: "If what you find is not true!" Sonnet "Methought that in a solemn church I stood."
11. Ch XI: Polwarth describes night visit to old house; heard woman and youth; found sheath; gives it to Wingfold.
12. Ch XII: Wingfold ponders "COME UNTO ME."
13. Ch XIII: Wingfold's Sunday sermon "Come unto me all ye that labour..."; Helen weeps.
14. Ch XIV: Wingfold's sonnet/poem "Yes, Master, when thou comest."
15. Ch XV: Bascombe criticises sermon; argues against God; Helen annoyed.
16. Ch XVI: Helen with Leopold; he sees Emmeline ("the jury").
17. Ch XVII: Helen plans to consult curate; sings "Come unto me" at piano.
18. Ch XVIII: Helen writes letter; Wingfold sets meeting at Polwarths'.
19. Ch XIX: Garden conversation: Helen veiled; Wingfold asks if she's a Christian ("No").
20. Ch XX: Helen faints; Polwarth prays; she flees.
21. Ch XXI: Helen alone in summer-house; proud, hates curate's counsel.
22. Ch XXII: Leopold sees Emmeline in mirror with worm on shoulder; begs to see Wingfold.
23. Ch XXIII: Helen brings Wingfold; he shows sheath; she begs him not to tell Leopold to confess; "I will trust you."
24. Ch XXIV: Leopold confesses to Wingfold, embraces him. Wingfold counsels Jesus.
25. Ch XXV: Wingfold: "I am with you always"; "Come unto me"; asks Leopold to ask forgiveness.
26. Ch XXVI: Wingfold walks out; Helen jealous; Leopold sleeps.
27. Ch XXVII: Second visit; Polwarth and Drew talk "Divine Service" (serving God through trade).
28. Ch XXVIII: Rachel reads "A Shop in Heaven" vision (economy of gift, prayer at shop).
29. Ch XXIX: Leopold resolves to give himself up; Polwarth affirms; Helen rebukes Wingfold; Leopold collapses.
30. Ch XXX: Bascombe visits; Leopold insists on confession; George plans magistrate Mr. Hooker on Monday.
31. Ch XXXI: George & Leopold talk of hanging; George goes to Helen.
32. Ch XXXII: Wingfold & Helen in library: "Then at least let your pride die for him."
33. Ch XXXIII: Wingfold's churchyard "curate's chair" meditation; poem "Father, I cry to thee for bread."
34. Ch XXXIV: Wingfold's sermon "He came not to call the righteous, but sinners." END OF VOLUME II.
